brief: BRIEF-3 (lower 48 US states), decisions 1-4 and rounds 2-3
revision: 2026-10-22/23: revised twice after two independent critics (PLAN-3.md 'Revision notes', first and second pass)
notes: Schedule (at most 3 agents at once): us-catalog, us-web and us-official start together (start_order 1). The first free slot goes to us-pipeline (start_order 2, the critical path to validation); it does M1 (weather quota) at once and starts its build-anywhere milestone only after the commit 'brief 3 us-catalog: M3' is in git log. Reviewers and fixers take the later free slots, one agent per slot, in the order the roles finished; never a 4th agent. Wave 2: validation, after every wave-1 role is reviewed, fixed and committed.

Commits: each milestone is committed as 'brief 3 <label>: M<n> <what>' with a pathspec (git add -- <new own paths> && git commit -m "..." -- <own paths>), so another role's staged files never ride along (CONTRACT 14.0). A gate failure confined to another role's file is recorded and rerun after that role's next commit.

Reviews: the reviewer reruns the role's acceptance checks in a clean worktree (git worktree add <scratch>/review-<label> HEAD; symlink web/node_modules; uv sync --offline; FIRE3D_DATA_DIR and FIRE3D_CACHE_DIR pointing at the main checkout's data/), on the role's own ports, and writes docs/redesign/reports/review3-<label>.json and docs/screenshots/review3-<label>-*.png (never the role's own evidence paths). The fixer owns the role's globs and commits with a pathspec.
Non-GET requests of a browser run are counted from the API's uvicorn access log: grep -cE '"(POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) ' <api log> (must be 0).
Every wave-1 role ends with a cut line; items below it that are not done go to the integration (PLAN-3 integration checklist) and are listed in the role's report.

The ownership globs ('owns') of wave 1 are disjoint (checked with the script in docs/redesign/PLAN-3.md appendix B against git ls-files plus the planned new files). Hand-offs are sequential: us-pipeline may update the build-gate tests in backend/tests/test_api.py only after us-catalog's review and fixes are committed. Wave 2 reuses paths that wave-1 roles owned ('owns' plus the bug-fix-only 'owns_bugfix_only' of validation); it runs alone.
Washington is not built (BRIEF-3 round 3 item 1): no Washington adapter, flag or certificate in any role.
As-built notes go to docs/redesign/contract3/<label>.md; CONTRACT.md is not edited in wave 1 (the integration folds the notes into section 14).

Glob syntax: '*' does not cross '/', '**' does, '[!abc]' excludes a first character (web/src/ui/shell/[!dLUo]* is every shell file except dataStatus*, LayersPanel.tsx, UpdatesPanel.tsx and officialSummary*; web/src/location/[!o]* is every location file except official* and openFromSearch.ts, which is listed on its own).

Wording scan (CONTRACT 14.0): every role lists and justifies each 'safe', 'low risk', 'all-clear' or reference-demo-name hit in the lines it added since the last 'brief 3 planner' commit; the integration and final verification scan the whole brief the same way.

**Goal.** Every wildfire of the lower 48 is listed and resolvable by id, with its state, time zone, issuer, region and record; the shared contracts exist for every other role; regions, the UTM rule, the national FIRMS feed, records, the accuracy seed and national search work offline-first. FIRMS (§14.12.1): `load_live_us`, `load_year_us` (pyarrow `filters=`, `firms_us_{year}.parquet`), deprecated CA wrappers, and every caller in your files switched: `firms._keyless` (`firms.py:736`, `:744`, used by `detections_for`), `catalog.py:252` and `:416`, `api/live.py:138` and `:163`. `api/live.py`: candidates from the national live list and feed (`fetch_cycle_data` on `load_live_us(days=7)`; 4 auto-builds, 100 ac, 48 h; §14.12.12), `LiveStatus.detections_24h` from `load_live_us(days=1)` inside the state polygons (keep `detections_24h_ca`). 6. **Cut line.** Below it, only after M1-M5 pass their checks; each item not done goes to the integration and is listed in your report with its fallback:
   - (a) ZCTA and county rows of the gazetteer ("83702", "83702 ID", "Ada County, ID"). Fallback: such a query answers the §14.10 no-match message.
   - (b) `backend/scripts/build_ca_county_gacc.py` → `ca_county_gacc.json`. Fallback: a California row not matched to a WFIGS record gets `accuracy_region: null` ("Accuracy not yet tested here").
   - (c) the scipy KD-tree in `catalog.assign_detections`. Fallback: today's matching, if it runs on the national feed in under 2 s (report the time).
   - (d) SPEC prose: §0 scope (lower 48), §2 rows from §14.13, §4.1 UTM rule, §4.2 ("The UI shows each fire's local time with its zone; Public 12-hour, Command and Forensic 24-hour"), §4.4 ids, §8.7 (live list). The §5.1/§6 rows are M1, above the line. `us-pipeline` sends its §8.2/§8.3/§8.4 text to the integration; do not wait for it.
   - (e) `backend/fire3d/data/nwcg_agency_codes.json` (check the wording and terms on NWCG's official Unit Identifier page; record source and date in `meta`; cite it in your report). Fallback: `agency` null for WFIGS rows; labels show the code verbatim ("USFS via NIFC WFIGS", §14.5).
   - (f) Id pinning (§14.2): a CAL FIRE row matched to a WFIGS record that already has a bundle under its WFIGS id keeps that id, with the CAL FIRE id in `aliases`, both ids resolving, and the 409 "'{alias}' is listed as '{id}'." for a build by the alias; test with a recorded before/after pair. Fallback: the old bundle stays reachable by its old link; the list shows the CAL FIRE row without it.

**New files.** Name new backend test files `backend/tests/test_us_catalog_*.py` (your glob); new samples go under `backend/tests/data/firedata/` or `backend/tests/data/regions/`.

**Not yours / deferred.** WFIGS change history outside California (B-R11) is deferred (the record says so). README is updated by final verification. No builds: never run `fire3d.cli build`, never press "Prepare analysis". `pipeline.is_catalog_incident` is `us-pipeline`'s; you provide `catalog.resolve_listed` for it.

New tests cover: every §14.3 point; the California merge regression set of §14.2 on recorded samples (Timber one row, active by NIFC, `other_records[0].source == 'wfigs'`; Alpaugh added; McCovey and Marshall separate; **Goal.** The map-first app works for the whole lower 48: a readable national overview with grouped markers, every time in the fire's own zone with the mixed clock (Public 12-hour, Command and Forensic 24-hour), national search and coverage messages, and the per-region accuracy label. CONTRACT §14.4 (wording, places), §14.5 (fire card), §14.9, §14.10 (web), §14.11, §14.12.6 are yours. You are a first-batch role: land M1 first; `us-official` depends on it.

**Ownership notes.** You own all of `web/src` except `web/src/api/**` (us-catalog), `official/**`, `extras/**`, `ui/feed/**`, `ui/shell/{officialSummary,dataStatus}*`, `ui/shell/UpdatesPanel.tsx`, `ui/shell/LayersPanel.tsx` and `location/official*` (us-official). Their exports that you call get optional `tf` shims (§14.9.6) from us-official; pass `tf` once they exist. The record label and the disagreement rule come from `web/src/api/records.ts` (`recordIssuerLabel`, `recordBlocks`; us-catalog M1): import them, never re-implement them. The new official lines of the location card arrive inside the existing `OfficialBlock.fireWeather` array (§14.7), so `location/CardParts.tsx`'s `OfficialSection` needs only its doc comment updated. 1. **M1, first 60 min.** `web/src/lib/time.ts` new API exactly as §14.9.2, deprecated names kept (§14.9.3); `web/src/lib/time.test.ts` (every row of the §14.9.2 table in both clocks; the six zones; DST start and end in America/New_York, America/Chicago, America/Denver, America/Phoenix; `wallTimeToMs` two-pass; `localWallTicks` hourly ticks on a DST day); `web/src/state/timeZone.ts` (`useZoneSource(): 'fire' | 'place' | 'viewer'`; + test of `clockFor`); `web/scripts/check-time-api.mjs` exactly as §14.9.3 (`--role <label>` from plan3-roles.json, skips `lib/time.ts`, import-based uses only, the `America/Los_Angeles` literal count with `// tz-ok:` opt-outs, exit 1 when either count is above 0).

roles.tasks:
**Goal.** Measure the fire-spread model outside California on 12 past fires (two per region; round 2 item 3), with California re-measured as the baseline, and publish honest per-region accuracy for the app. Follow `docs/redesign/audit-3/validation.md` §3-§5 (fires, ids, starts, protocol, label) and CONTRACT §14.4 (file schema) exactly. You are the only agent in wave 2 and may build fires with the CLI, one at a time, in the background.

**Ownership.** Your own work: `spread/**`, `build/weather_bundle.py` (GSI series, the interim warning), `sources/weather.py`, `config.py`, `regional_accuracy.json`, `backend/scripts/validate_*.py`, the GSI and aggregation tests, `docs/validation.md`. **Bug fixes only** in the build code you exercise (`build/**`, `sources/{landfire,perimeters,terrain,firms}.py`, `catalog.py`, `cli.py`, `types.py` and their tests): each fix with a regression test, listed in your report with the file, the cause and the before/after effect. Read `docs/redesign/contract3/*.md` where present; SPEC.md is not yours (write SPEC text in `notes_for_integrator`).

**Steps.**
0. **Weather first.** Before every build: `uv run python -m fire3d.cli weather-probe`. If `overall` is not `ok`, wait for the reset (about 00:00 UTC) and probe again; never build with ERA5 fill (`--require-hrrr` on every build). If the cap blocks for more than a day, tell the orchestrator (V §7 option A is the default; B and C need the user).
1. **California baseline** (V-R14, protocol step 0): build `2025-madre-fire-01e7e8` (with `--require-hrrr`, so a refused water-year request fails the build; its bundle must have `sim/antecedent.json` with `precip_wy_mm`); re-run the 31-member p50 hindcasts at docs/validation.md's starts on Eaton, Madre and Palisades; record per-fire and 32-lead values next to §5.1 (0.438 / 0.395 / 0.467), and each fire's (herb, woody) values. A difference over 0.02 caused by brief-3 code (perimeters, fuels, time zones, issuer text, weather handling) is a regression: fix it with a test before going on. A difference from other causes (for example revised upstream weather or perimeters) is explained with evidence.
2. **Pre-register** (V-R5, protocol step 3), in a new docs/validation.md section, **committed before any non-California hindcast**:
   - the GSI method exactly as CONTRACT §14.12.10: the NFDRS 2016 Growing Season Index (Jolly et al. 2005), its parameters, the herb/woody mapping, with citations; the switch on `summary.state` (`"CA"` keeps today's method); the inputs, start − 28 d to start: daily ERA5 minimum/maximum temperature, vapour pressure deficit or dew point and day length from the archive host for historical builds (about 2 call units), and the same daily variables from the forecast host with `past_days=28` for live builds (ERA5 lags about 6 days);
   - **absolute UTC starts for all 12 fires**: V §3's times, and for Horse Gulch, Greer and Rush (listed there as "ignition + 6, 12, 24 h", Greer also 72 h) the WFIGS `FireDiscoveryDateTime` plus those offsets, written out as UTC; the ignition-relative secondary times (+6/12/24 h) of every fire are computed the same way and written out too, so no start depends on a bundle's computed `ignition.t_ms`;
   - the replacement rule of step 3.
   Then implement GSI: the daily requests in `sources/weather.py` (historical and live), the series stored as the backend-only `sim/lfm_gsi.json` (no SPEC contract change; hindcasts never fetch), GSI for fires outside California in `spread/moisture.py` / `ensemble.py` / `behavior.py`, California unchanged, the interim warning of §14.12.10 removed in `build/weather_bundle.py` where GSI applies, never a silent fallback (a non-California bundle without the series uses California's values with the warning and the moisture note, `lfm_method` `ca_month_table` or `ca_month_table_drought`), `require_hrrr=True` failing the build on a refused GSI series, `lfm_method` recorded. Tests against the method's published reference values, the never-silent fallback, the `require_hrrr` failure, and the unchanged California (herb, woody) values and moisture note for Eaton, Palisades, Madre (bundles when present) and `fixture-demo`. **Then re-run California**: the 31-member p50 on Eaton, Madre and Palisades at the step 1 starts must equal step 1 (|Δ| < 0.001 per fire and over the 32 leads; seeds are fixed); report both side by side; any difference is a bug, fixed with a test before any non-California hindcast. After the first non-California score, only bug fixes, each with before/after values for every fire. Write the SPEC §8.4 GSI paragraph in `notes_for_integrator`.
3. **Build the 12 fires** of V §3 by their proposed ids, each with `--require-hrrr` (Horse Gulch and Black Cove are `--force` rebuilds of the smoke bundles, or first builds if `us-pipeline` left them "pending (quota)", in which case you also take over their wave-1 checks and screenshots). Run the bundle checks of protocol step 2 for each and record them (area ratio 0.8-1.25, perimeters in the growth window, fire inside the AOI, `fuels_edition` per V §3, UTM zone per V §3, 0 ERA5 hours, no observed pixel > 2 km outside the fire's own final WFIGS perimeter), plus the weather source and the GFS fill hours (hours with `hrrr` false): the source should be `open-meteo:historical-forecast:gfs_hrrr`; any fill hours are reported with where they fall relative to the scored windows and justified. **Replacement rule** (pre-registered): a fire is replaced only when it fails a bundle check, before any of its scores exist, by the next reserve of the same region in V §3's order; the failed check is recorded (`replaced` in the file). Southern Plains has no reserve: if Windy Deuce or Rush fails, that region is `limited` (or `untested`). Nothing else justifies a replacement.
4. **Hindcasts** (protocol steps 4-7): the absolute UTC starts pre-registered in step 2 (Windy Deuce's revised starts included), operational settings, `--adjustments 0.5`; the deterministic member and the 31-member p50; leads 12/24/48/72 h; the ignition + 6/12/24 h secondary score for every fire; the California-table ablation outside the label; pseudo-live where FIRMS and CMR allow. No tuning to these fires unless it also improves California (report everything tried); an adopted change sets `in_sample: true` (with §14.4's in-sample wording) for every region whose fires informed it.
5. **Regional aggregation** (V-R9): `validate regional` in `spread/validate.py` (mean of fire means, pooled and ignition-relative values, `by_lead` keyed "12"/"24"/"48"/"72", growth ratio, `fuel_groups_tested`, statuses by the §14.4 rule: `tested` with >= 2 fires and >= 16 leads, otherwise `limited` with >= 1 fire, `untested` with 0) writing `backend/fire3d/data/regional_accuracy.json` (schema §14.4 incl. `gfs_fill_hours`, `weather_source` and `replaced` per fire, `seed` absent, OSCC from the post-GSI California re-run and `in_sample: true`, RMCC/EACC/ONCC `untested`), with tests.
6. **docs/validation.md**: a new section with per-fire, per-lead and per-region results, sample sizes, the California baseline, the GSI ablation, and honest caveats (Windy Deuce scores only the second day; Lower Sugarloaf's run is VIIRS-timed; Rush's first perimeter is 46 %; small samples, about ±0.05). Times in UTC plus each fire's local zone.

**Acceptance checks (a reviewer reruns these in a clean worktree, PLAN-3 "Reviews").**
- [ ] `cd backend && uv run pytest -q` passes, with new tests for GSI (reference values), the never-silent fallback, `require_hrrr` failing on a refused GSI series, California (herb, woody) values unchanged by the GSI code (Eaton, Palisades, Madre, `fixture-demo`), the aggregation (mean of fire means; `limited` with 1 fire and with 2 fires under 16 leads; `untested` with 0) and the JSON schema; a regression test for every bug fix in the build code.
- [ ] California unchanged after GSI: the post-GSI re-run of Eaton, Madre and Palisades equals step 1 (|Δ| < 0.001 per fire and over the 32 leads), shown side by side in the report and in docs/validation.md.
- [ ] `git log --format='%h %s' -- docs/validation.md` shows the pre-registration commit before the first commit with non-California hindcast results, and that commit lists absolute UTC starts for all 12 fires (none written as "ignition + …"), both GSI inputs (historical and live) and the replacement rule.
- [ ] `backend/fire3d/data/regional_accuracy.json`: 10 regions; each tested region has 2 fires; every fire has `era5_hours: 0`, the `fuels_edition` of V §3, `weather_source` `open-meteo:historical-forecast:gfs_hrrr` or reported and justified `gfs_fill_hours`, and `replaced` set for any replacement; every fire outside California has `lfm_method: "gsi_nfdrs2016"`; Madre's bundle has `sim/antecedent.json` with `precip_wy_mm`; OSCC from the post-GSI re-run; `in_sample: true` wherever a change was adopted; no `seed` key.
- [ ] API on 8716 (`FIRE3D_LIVE=0`): `/api/accuracy-regions` serves the new file.
- [ ] The weather-probe lines before every build are in the report; 13 builds (Madre + the 12 fires, among them the `--force` rebuilds of Horse Gulch and Black Cove), plus any reserve builds, listed with duration and bundle-check results.
- [ ] Web gates still pass (you change no web file).
